summary: Retest of HIGH-priority fix: completed-service un-complete guard for non-admin PATCH. Updated /app/backend/tests/test_production_qa.py TestLLocking class to add 7 targeted assertions per the review request. All 50 tests pass (0 failed, 0 skipped). Verified: (1) technician PATCH {status:'pending'} on OWN completed service is blocked (returns 400 'Nothing to update' after allowed-set filter reduces upd to {}) AND DB status stays 'completed'. (2) technician PATCH {payment_status:'paid'} on completed service returns 200 and persists; toggling back to 'unpaid' also 200. (3) mixed {status:'pending', payment_status:'paid'} by technician on completed returns 200 with only payment_status applied — DB status remains 'completed' (acceptable per spec). (4) manager PATCH {status:'pending'} → 400, {charges:5} → 400 (charges stripped by manager branch then upd empty → 400), {payment_status:'paid'} → 200. (5) admin PATCH {charges:2000, payment_status:'paid'} on completed → 200 and BOTH fields persist. Regression: all prior scenarios still pass — end-to-end Termite auto-reminder creation (due_date ≈ +365-7d), termite duplicate prevention, non-termite no reminder, manager permissions & financial stripping, technician permissions & filters, admin edits + audit, AMC generation for daily/fortnightly/monthly/quarterly/custom, AMC contract has null technician_id, reassignment flips pending→assigned, reschedule future=rescheduled/past=overdue, /reports/summary admin-only, CSV export (200/401/403), /files with token, manager dashboard pending_payments, MongoDB persistence, _id never leaked.

minor.issue: When a technician sends only disallowed fields (e.g. {status:'pending'} on a completed service), server returns 400 'Nothing to update'. Semantically fine but a 403 'Cannot un-complete' would be clearer for API consumers. Non-blocking.
Response body still contains 'charges' key (forced to 0). Not a leak but asymmetric with GET which strips it.
Any valid JWT (any role) can read any object path if guessed. Prefix + ownership check recommended.
No content-type whitelist and no size cap on uploads.
No pagination cursor, no filters, no index on 'at' — will slow at scale.

action_items: None blocking. Optional: change 'Nothing to update' 400 to a more explicit 403 with body {detail:'Cannot un-complete service'} when a technician sends only disallowed fields on a completed service.
Optional MINOR items unchanged from iteration_5: strip 'charges' from manager POST response; harden /files endpoint; add upload validation; audit-logs pagination.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py update_service (lines 447-485): fix is correct and minimal — for technicians on completed services, allowed-set is reduced to {'payment_status'} only, so any attempt to PATCH 'status' (alone or mixed) is silently filtered and either 400 ('Nothing to update') or 200 with only payment_status applied. Status field is provably unreachable for technicians on completed services.
Verified admin branch remains fully permissive (no completed-lock for role=='admin').
Manager on completed: only 'payment_status' allowed; other fields → 400 'Service completed and locked'. Matches spec.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_production_qa.py (expanded TestLLocking from 2 tests to 8 tests covering the fix + regression)

rca_of_issue: PREVIOUS BUG (fixed in this iteration): Technician could un-complete a service. Root cause was server.py update_service technician branch not checking completed status. FIX APPLIED at server.py:453-464 — when user role is technician AND s.get('status')=='completed', the allowed-fields set is restricted to {'payment_status'} only (Cash Collection), preventing any status/medicine/quantity/notes changes post-completion. VERIFIED via 7 new pytest assertions: status un-complete attempts by tech and manager return 4xx and DB state remains 'completed'; payment_status toggling still works for tech/manager; admin remains fully unlocked.
